location: Boundaries > Always > Docs (4th interim rule: 'a cell in its `appended`' ... 'the run exited 143'); I/O row 'Stop'
issue: The infra-cause test is keyed on the cells in the run's `appended` list, and it names the exit-143 case explicitly. An exit-143 run prints no output line, though. `run_e2e` returns 143 before `_e2e_exit`, and `test_e2e_stopped` asserts 'exit 143, tanpa baris output'. So after a stop that Budi asks to rerun, the orchestrator has no `appended` list. Records from the done-child path (for example a `crash` or `no-slots` written before the stop) can never be recognised as an infra cause, and the environment prompt is skipped. The 'Stop' row also does not say whether a stopped run prints the line.
implementation_impact: The docs writer cannot implement the rule for the 143 path. An implementer may add an output line on stop that the contract (`ran`|`skipped`) does not define, or break the existing 'no output line' test without guidance.
suggestion: Pin one source for the cells a stopped run appended. Either have the stop path log the appended cells to stderr (as the append-error path already does with 'rekaman yang sudah di-append: ...') and let the docs read them from there, or say that on exit 143 the infra check reads the records carrying the run's Job ID. State in the 'Stop' row that no output line is printed.

location: Boundaries > Always > Docs (4th interim rule: infra cause read from 'the next plan's e2e `rerun_matrix` reason')
issue: `cell_reason` takes its `inconclusive`/`inconclusive-steps`/`browser-notes` reasons from the cell's newest FRESH record. Suppose the module changes after the run started (an edit during a multi-hour run, or a patch before the next plan call). The run's records are then stale and the reason becomes `stale-source`, so the infra cause is silently lost and no environment prompt appears. Each patch also changes the fingerprint, so `blocked-infra` (same fingerprint required) never trips. The orchestrator can therefore rerun into the same missing image or missing browser again and again without ever asking Budi.
implementation_impact: The interactive retry guard is defeated in exactly the case where runs are long. The docs rule passes review, but the signal it reads does not depend on what the run produced.
suggestion: Define 'left an infra cause' from the run's own records (history lines with this run's `job_id`/`run_id`), using the same infra-cause function as plan step 3, whatever their freshness. Or have the plan expose that per-record cause so the docs do not infer it from the rerun reason.

location: Boundaries > Always > Runner ('A stop never lands between a record's write and its bookkeeping: it is deferred around each append')
issue: Deferring the stop around each single append does not make a child's reap atomic. In `loop()` a finished future is popped from `self.running` and only then passed to `_on_reaped`, which appends one record per engine and then decides fail-fast. A stop can land (a) after the pop and before `_on_reaped`, or (b) between the chromium and firefox appends of the same child. In (a) the child is no longer in `running`, so the 'future is done()' rule may miss it, and its real result (possibly a `fail`) is replaced by `stopped`. In (b) the done-child rule either appends chromium a second time or firefox gets `stopped` although its parsed result was in hand. A stop inside `_unstarted_records` also leaves a partial set of `not-run` records.
implementation_impact: The 'at most one record per admitted cell' guarantee and 'real results kept' can both be broken. The listed test (a stop injected mid-append, one record) does not cover the multi-engine child or the pop-to-reap gap.
suggestion: Defer the stop across the whole reap of one child: pop, every record, bookkeeping and the fail-fast decision, and also across a fail-fast/no-slots batch. Or state that the stop path re-processes a child taken off `running` and not yet fully reaped, skipping cells that already have a record this run. Add a test with a two-engine child stopped between its two appends.

location: Boundaries > Always > Runner (run's own stop: 'every other admitted cell without a record this run (tracked per cell) gets `stopped`')
issue: Take a child whose future is done() at stop time and that exited 2 or reported `status: skipped`. By contract it leaves no record, and the spec keeps 'zero records for an exit-2 or skipped child'. Its cells are still admitted cells 'without a record this run', so the catch-all writes `stopped` for them. This contradicts the zero-record rule. For the skipped case it also turns a 'Playwright/Docker absent' outcome into an inconclusive history line, which the next plan reads as reason `inconclusive`, a candidate infra cause.
implementation_impact: Two rules in the same bullet give different answers for the same cell. Whichever the implementer picks, one of the listed tests ('zero records for an exit-2 or skipped child', or the stop test) will disagree with the spec.
suggestion: Exclude from the stop path's `stopped` catch-all the cells of a done child with rc 2 or a `skipped` payload: no record, and exit stays 143. Add that case to the run-stop test.

location: Boundaries > Always > Runner (stop path appends after `JobStopped`)
issue: The SIGTERM handler (`fl._on_sigterm`) stays armed while the stop path runs. A second SIGTERM can come from a repeated `--stop-job`, from the headless silent-log rule together with an operator, or from `stop_job` targeting several registry entries of the same job. It raises `JobStopped` inside the stop path's own appends. The exception then escapes to `_run()`, which returns 143, and the remaining in-flight cells never get their `stopped` records. The spec covers append errors on the stop path but not a re-entrant stop.
implementation_impact: Cells end up with no record for that run, which breaks 'exactly one per admitted cell'. The orchestrator then sees reasons left over from older records.
suggestion: State that the handler is disarmed (or made to set a flag only) once the stop is being handled, so later SIGTERMs are ignored until exit 143. Add a test that raises a second `JobStopped` during the first stopped append.

issue: The deferral and stop-path work needs code the Code Map does not list. In ps-flashlight-run that is `_on_sigterm` and `job_register`: the handler that raises `JobStopped`, installed for flashlight, scenario and E2E children as well. In ps-run-layer it is `_SlotRun._append`, `loop`, `_unstarted_records`, `_e2e_exit` and `_run`. The spec says only what must not happen ('a main-thread pthread_sigmask alone does not do it'). It does not say whether the mechanism is a ps-run-layer-local handler or a change to the shared one.
implementation_impact: An implementer may patch the shared `_on_sigterm`, which changes stop behaviour in every Docker layer child, out of this slice's scope and without tests there. Or they may miss `loop`/`_unstarted_records`, where the unprotected windows are.
suggestion: Add those symbols to the Code Map and pin the mechanism. For example, ps-run-layer installs its own SIGTERM handler after `job_register`; inside a critical section it records a pending stop, and it raises `JobStopped` when the section ends. ps-flashlight-run's handler stays unchanged for the children.

location: Boundaries > Always > Runner ('appended from the stop path without waiting for the children')
issue: In the current code ps-run-layer cannot leave without waiting. Children run in a `ThreadPoolExecutor`, and `shutdown(wait=False)` does not stop `concurrent.futures`' atexit hook from joining worker threads that are blocked in `_spawn`. The process (and its live registry entry) stays until every child exits. Meanwhile the `finally` block removes `run.tmp` while children may still write their `-o` output there. When the SIGTERM did not come from `--stop-job`, so the children were not signalled, this lasts until the children finish, and their real results are discarded after `stopped` was already written.
implementation_impact: The 'without waiting' wording can be read as permission to `os._exit` or to use daemon threads (skipping atexit, registry cleanup and log flushing), or as satisfied when it is not. `--list-jobs` keeps showing a 'stopped' run as alive.
suggestion: Say what 'without waiting' means: the records are written before any join, and exit 143 is returned after the existing atexit and registry cleanup. Also state whether the tmp directory is kept until the children exit, or accept that late child writes fail.

location: Boundaries > Always > Docs (Headless: 'stop at the first unclean step, `reached`/`not reached`, `e2e_tier_reached`')
issue: The contract defines `e2e_tier_reached` as '{tier, step} from the last plan call', and headless judges a step clean 'after the run'. The spec does not say which plan call that is. If headless re-plans after a run to judge cleanliness (the only script source for it), then after a tier-1 gate failure the last plan derives `focus` (tier 0) for the failing cell. The return then reports `e2e_tier_reached: {tier: 0, step: focus}` and 'not reached: stopped at focus', although tier 1 ran and produced the failure. After a canary failure both calls say `focus`, so only the gate case misreports.
implementation_impact: Headless callers (psm-develop, psm-optimize baselines) get a tier and step that understate how far validation went. The four caller docs then report a gate failure as a fix-loop stop.
suggestion: Pin `e2e_tier_reached` to the plan call whose step was last run (or found blocked), and pin cleanliness to the post-run plan's `rerun_matrix` entries for that step's `e2e_next_cells`. Add a docs criterion for the gate-failure case.

location: Boundaries > Always > Docs (4th interim rule: 'before the next E2E run after one that left an infra cause ..., whatever its step')
issue: Firing the environment prompt before ANY next run, whatever its step, goes beyond 'before an infra retry'. The interim scoped it per version: an infra retry of V was pending until V's next E2E run. Example: a gate run leaves 1.7.8:firefox `no-slots` and fails 8.1:chromium. The next step is a loop-back `focus` on 8.1:chromium, which does not drive 1.7.8 at all. Budi is still asked to fix the 1.7.8 environment first, and a decline ends the whole E2E loop, killing an unrelated fix loop.
implementation_impact: The docs will either end E2E for a session over an infra cause the next run cannot hit, or give the orchestrator reason to drift from the written rule.
suggestion: Prompt only when the next step's `e2e_next_cells` include a cell (or a version) that left the infra cause. Otherwise carry the cause forward until such a step comes, as the interim's 'infra retry of V pending' did.

location: Boundaries > Always > Docs (Headless: 'config copy with canary reset, only for a well-formed canary outside the set, a malformed one kept') and AC 3
issue: The LLM orchestrator, not a script, writes the copy. It must tell 'well-formed but outside the caller's cells' apart from 'malformed' by re-implementing the normalizer in prose: whole-value trim, a single `:`, per-part trim, browser case-folding, an exact configured version string, `chromium`/`firefox`/`webkit` only. `9.1:Chromium `, `9.1.0:chromium` (exact match against which set?) or `9.1:webkit` with webkit unconfigured are easy to misclassify. One mistake either blocks a valid headless call or resets a broken config and hides it.
implementation_impact: The rule is untestable by the Verification commands, and it duplicates the normalizer's rules outside their single owner.
suggestion: Give the docs a script signal. Have the normalizer distinguish 'malformed' from 'outside configured cells' in its exit-2 message (a stable prefix naming `psm_e2e_canary`). Headless then writes the copy, runs the plan, and resets the canary only when the plan's stderr reports the 'outside' kind. Or add a tiny check mode to the plan.

location: Tasks > tests (run-stop test with `--slots 3` and four versions)
issue: The test leaves the outcome of the 'one reaped' version unstated. If its child appended a `fail`, fail-fast fires before the stop and writes `not-run` for the queued version, contradicting the expected 'nothing for the queued one'. Four versions also need a config with four `psm_target_versions`; the test helpers' default config is 3×n, and the spec does not say so.
implementation_impact: Different fixtures give contradictory expectations, so the test can be written to pass for the wrong reason or fail against a correct implementation.
suggestion: State that the reaped version's child passes (no fail-fast before the stop) and that the test uses a four-version config. Also assert the 'one reaped' records are untouched by the stop path.
